paragraphs.text: A loose [red tea](red:definition) from [Yuchi](yuchi:where-it-is), the township that holds Sun Moon Lake in the middle of Nantou County. Red tea took root here under Japanese rule, when the colonial government wanted it for export and brought in [large leaf Assam seed](yuchi:assam-planting) from India. Of the trial sites, Yuchi was the one that did well, because its [warm, misty basin](yuchi:why-red-tea), deep reddish soil and steady lake weather were likened to the Assam country itself.

This leaf dates from 1980, when that export trade was [fading](yuchi:decline-and-return): from the 1970s rising wages made hand picked leaf costly against red tea from other countries, and many growers moved to oolong or to other crops. The style has [no tradition of ageing](red:ageing). Sealed, it is expected to keep its quality for a year and a half to three years, so at forty-six years this tea sits far outside the life the trade gives it.

brewing.text: Red tea takes water near the boil, about 90 to 100°C; hotter water draws out its aroma and flavour more fully, but its bitterness faster too. In a pot or mug, use about a rounded spoon of leaf for each cup and steep three to five minutes, less for broken leaf and a little less, and a little cooler, for a light, delicate tea. Left too long, it turns bitter and drying, because time and heat pull more tannins from the leaf.

notice.text: A sweet cup, often with honey, floral or fruity notes, malt in many, and a brisk strength in the stronger teas. The liquor runs red, bright to deep.
